topic.title: Suggesting Changes to a Project
topic.shortdesc: Contributors propose their changes to a project by creating a review task from the changes in their personal workspace.

body.p: By creating a review task, a Contributor submits a set of changes to the project team. The task contains your changes, which project maintainers and owners review to decide whether to integrate them into the project.

section.title: Proposing Your Changes
section.p: To suggest changes to a project:

ol.li: Open the project and edit the files you want to change in your personal workspace.
Select the Changes view in the left stripe to view the files you modified.
Make sure that all your changed files are included. A review task is always created from the complete set of changes in your workspace.
Click New Review Task.Deleted and renamed files cannot be sent for review. If your changes include any, revert them before you create the task.
Enter a title for the task in the field at the top of the pane, then click the check mark on the right when you are done.
Optionally, enter a Description, specify a Due Date, or select a Context Publication so that the files are rendered as a hierarchical tree.
Click Create to create the task.

section.p: Result: The review task is created, and your changes are no longer limited to your workspace. The task is created without an owner and waits for a project maintainer or owner to take it over. For details, see After You Suggest Changes.

ul.li: Keep each proposal focused on a single subject. Because the task includes every change in your workspace, unrelated edits are included in the same review.
Give the task a title that explains what you changed and why, so the project team can understand the proposal before opening it.
Use the task description to provide any information reviewers need, such as the source of information you corrected.
